message.content: {"appearance_facts": [{"location": "The color scale legend on the right side of the page", "fact": "The scale is inverted relative to typical heatmaps; the top is labeled 'High' with a value of 100 and a pale yellow color, while the bottom is labeled 'Low' with a value of 0 and a dark maroon color."}, {"location": "The state of Idaho (ID) in the upper-left region", "fact": "The state is filled with a very pale yellow color, corresponding to the 'High' end of the legend."}, {"location": "The state of South Carolina (SC) in the mid-right region", "fact": "The state is filled with a dark maroon color, corresponding to the 'Low' end of the legend."}, {"location": "The state of Arizona (AZ) in the lower-left region", "fact": "The state is filled with a solid light gray color, distinct from the yellow-to-maroon gradient used for the other states."}, {"location": "Comparing the three option states", "fact": "Idaho (ID) is the lightest yellow of the three, South Carolina (SC) is the darkest maroon, and Arizona (AZ) is gray."}], "printed_facts": [{"location": "Top left corner", "fact": "The title reads 'Risk Index of Hazard H in US States'."}, {"location": "Right side", "fact": "The legend shows a vertical gradient bar with 'High' at the top (100) and 'Low' at the bottom (0)."}, {"location": "State labels", "fact": "The labels 'ID', 'SC', and 'AZ' are printed within their respective state boundaries."}], "public_definitions": [], "uncertain": ["The specific numerical value for each state is not printed on the map, only the color gradient is visible.", "The meaning of the gray color (used for AZ, CA, NM, etc.) is not explicitly defined in the legend, which only shows the yellow-to-maroon gradient."]}
